english.title: Make insurance document with intent to deceive
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), with intent to deceive, made a

(A)_[document]_
(B)_[thing]_

so closely resembling a

(C)_[certificate of insurance]_
(D)_[certificate of security under part VI of the Road Traffic Act 1988]_
(E)_[document produced as evidence of compulsory insurance pursuant to regulation 6 of the Motor Vehicles (Compulsory Insurance)(No 2) Regulations 1973]_
(F)_[document issued under regulations made by virtue of the power under section 165(2)(a) of the Road Traffic Act 1988]_

as to be calculated to deceive
english.legislation: Contrary to section 173(1)(c) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) See also offence wordings: H2519, H2520, H3023, H3025, H3027, H3029 and H3031.
(ii) From 1st November 2019, the Motor Vehicles (Compulsory Insurance) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2019 (SI 2019/1047) removed the current securities regime, which was used as an alternative to conventional motor insurance. A two-year transitional period applied to existing securities and deposits; this meant that new securities could not be issued, however, it did not prevent individuals renewing current securities - as long as they were valid until 1st November 2021. From 1st November 2021 compulsory motor insurance is required. For the offence applying from this date, see H100118.

other.penalty:
Either way

SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
